docs.title: Filters & Tags
docs.text: TemplateTo extends Liquid with custom filters and tags for document generation. These work alongside standard Liquid filters.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Filters transform values. Apply them with the pipe (|) character:

{{ value | filter_name }}
{{ value | filter_name: argument }}

docs.title: parse_date
docs.text:
Converts a string to a date object, which you can then format with the date filter.

Syntax: 

{{ string | parse_date }}
{{ string | parse_date: true }}  <!-- US date format (MM/DD/YY) -->

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description isUS boolean false Set to true for US date format (MM/DD/YY)

Examples:

<!-- European format (DD/MM/YY) - default -->
{{ "15/11/23" | parse_date | date: "%e %B %Y" }}
<!-- Result: 15 November 2023 -->

<!-- US format (MM/DD/YY) -->
{{ "11/15/23" | parse_date: true | date: "%e %B %Y" }}
<!-- Result: 15 November 2023 -->

<!-- Different output formats -->
{{ "15/11/23" | parse_date | date: "%Y-%m-%d" }}
<!-- Result: 2023-11-15 -->

{{ "15/11/23" | parse_date | date: "%d/%m/%Y" }}
<!-- Result: 15/11/2023 -->

Date Format Reference

Use strftime.net to build date format strings interactively.

Common date format codes:

Code Description Example %Y 4-digit year 2023 %y 2-digit year 23 %m Month (01-12) 11 %B Full month name November %b Short month name Nov %d Day (01-31) 15 %e Day (1-31, space-padded) 15 %H Hour (00-23) 14 %I Hour (01-12) 02 %M Minute (00-59) 30 %p AM/PM PM

docs.title: format_number
docs.text:
Formats numbers using .NET standard numeric format strings.

Syntax: 

{{ number | format_number: "format_string" }}

Examples:

<!-- Currency -->
{{ 1234.5 | format_number: "C" }}
<!-- Result: $1,234.50 (depends on culture) -->

<!-- Fixed decimal places -->
{{ 123 | format_number: "N" }}
<!-- Result: 123.00 -->

{{ 123.456 | format_number: "N2" }}
<!-- Result: 123.46 -->

<!-- Percentage -->
{{ 0.25 | format_number: "P" }}
<!-- Result: 25.00% -->

<!-- Custom format -->
{{ 1234567.89 | format_number: "#,##0.00" }}
<!-- Result: 1,234,567.89 -->

Common format specifiers:

Format Description Example Input Example Output N Number with thousand separators 1234.5 1,234.50 N0 Number, no decimals 1234.5 1,235 N2 Number, 2 decimals 1234.5 1,234.50 C Currency 1234.5 $1,234.50 C0 Currency, no decimals 1234.5 $1,235 P Percentage 0.25 25.00% P0 Percentage, no decimals 0.256 26% F2 Fixed-point, 2 decimals 1234.5 1234.50

Culture-Aware Formatting

Currency symbols and separators depend on the template's culture settings. For example, C displays $ for en-US but £ for en-GB.

docs.title: to_number
docs.text:
Converts a string to a number. Useful when your JSON contains numbers as strings.

Syntax: 

{{ string | to_number }}

Examples:

<!-- Convert string to number for calculations -->
{% assign price = "99.99" | to_number %}
{% assign quantity = "3" | to_number %}
{% assign total = price | times: quantity %}
{{ total }}
<!-- Result: 299.97 -->

<!-- Use with format_number -->
{{ "1234.5" | to_number | format_number: "C" }}
<!-- Result: $1,234.50 -->

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Tags provide logic and control flow. They use {% %} syntax.

docs.title: secUp
docs.text:
Increments and displays a section counter. The counter only increments when the tag is actually rendered (useful with conditional content).

Syntax: 

{% secUp counterName %}

Example:

<h2>{% secUp mainSection %}. Introduction</h2>
<!-- Output: 1. Introduction -->

{% if showMethods %}
<h2>{% secUp mainSection %}. Methods</h2>
<!-- Output: 2. Methods (only if showMethods is true) -->
{% endif %}

<h2>{% secUp mainSection %}. Conclusion</h2>
<!-- Output: 2. Conclusion (if Methods was skipped) -->
<!-- Output: 3. Conclusion (if Methods was shown) -->

Counter Names

You can use any name for your counter. Use different names for different numbering sequences (e.g., mainSection, subSection, figure).

docs.title: secCt
docs.text:
Returns the current value of a section counter without incrementing it.

Syntax: 

{% secCt counterName %}

Example:

<h2>{% secUp mainSection %}. Introduction</h2>
<!-- Output: 1. Introduction -->

<h3>{% secCt mainSection %}.1 Background</h3>
<!-- Output: 1.1 Background -->

<h3>{% secCt mainSection %}.2 Objectives</h3>
<!-- Output: 1.2 Objectives -->

<h2>{% secUp mainSection %}. Methods</h2>
<!-- Output: 2. Methods -->

docs.title: Combining Filters
docs.text:
Chain multiple filters together:

<!-- Parse date, then format it -->
{{ order.date | parse_date | date: "%B %d, %Y" }}

<!-- Convert to number, multiply, then format as currency -->
{{ item.price | to_number | times: item.quantity | format_number: "C" }}

docs.title: Liquid Reference
docs.text: TemplateTo uses the Liquid templating language. This page provides a quick reference for common syntax.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Insert values using double curly braces:

{{ variable }}
{{ object.property }}
{{ array[0] }}

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Transform values with filters (pipe syntax):

{{ name | upcase }}
{{ price | round: 2 }}
{{ text | truncate: 50 }}
{{ items | size }}

Chain multiple filters:

{{ name | downcase | capitalize }}
{{ date | parse_date | date: "%Y-%m-%d" }}

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags provide logic. They don't output anything directly.

{% if condition %}...{% endif %}
{% for item in array %}...{% endfor %}
{% assign variable = value %}

docs.title: if / elsif / else
docs.text:
{% if customer.tier == "gold" %}
    <span class="gold-badge">Gold Member</span>
{% elsif customer.tier == "silver" %}
    <span class="silver-badge">Silver Member</span>
{% else %}
    <span>Standard Member</span>
{% endif %}

docs.title: unless
docs.text:
The opposite of if:

{% unless order.shipped %}
    <p>Order is being processed</p>
{% endunless %}

docs.title: case / when
docs.text:
{% case status %}
    {% when "pending" %}
        <span class="yellow">Pending</span>
    {% when "approved" %}
        <span class="green">Approved</span>
    {% when "rejected" %}
        <span class="red">Rejected</span>
    {% else %}
        <span>Unknown</span>
{% endcase %}

docs.title: Comparison
Logical
Contains
docs.text:
Check if string contains substring, or array contains value:

{% if email contains "@company.com" %}
    Internal user
{% endif %}

{% if tags contains "urgent" %}
    <span class="urgent">!</span>
{% endif %}

docs.title: for loop
docs.text:
{% for product in products %}
    <div>{{ product.name }}</div>
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Loop parameters
docs.text:
<!-- Limit to 5 items -->
{% for item in items limit:5 %}

<!-- Skip first 2 items -->
{% for item in items offset:2 %}

<!-- Reverse order -->
{% for item in items reversed %}

docs.title: forloop object
docs.text:
{% for item in items %}
    {{ forloop.index }}     <!-- 1, 2, 3... -->
    {{ forloop.index0 }}    <!-- 0, 1, 2... -->
    {{ forloop.first }}     <!-- true on first -->
    {{ forloop.last }}      <!-- true on last -->
    {{ forloop.length }}    <!-- total items -->
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Range loops
docs.text:
{% for i in (1..5) %}
    {{ i }}
{% endfor %}
<!-- Output: 1 2 3 4 5 -->

docs.title: Empty fallback

{% for item in items %}
    {{ item.name }}
{% else %}
    No items found.
{% endfor %}

docs.text:
{% for item in items %}
    {% if item.hidden %}
        {% continue %}
    {% endif %}

    {{ item.name }}

    {% if forloop.index > 10 %}
        {% break %}
    {% endif %}
{% endfor %}

{{ greeting }}, {{ fullName }}!

{{ street }}

docs.title: Localization
docs.text: TemplateTo supports culture-aware formatting for numbers, currencies, and dates. Set the culture to control how values are displayed for different regions.

docs.title: Setting Culture
docs.text: Culture is set per-render via the API or template settings. The culture name follows the standard format: language-REGION (e.g., en-US, en-GB, de-DE).

docs.title: Via API
docs.text:
Include cultureName in your render request:

{
  "templateId": "tpl_abc123",
  "data": { ... },
  "cultureName": "en-GB"
}

docs.title: Via Template Settings
docs.text: Set a default culture in your template's settings for consistent formatting.

docs.title: Currency Formatting
docs.text:
The format_number: "C" filter uses the culture's currency symbol and format:

Culture {{ 1234.50 \| format_number: "C" }} en-US $1,234.50 en-GB £1,234.50 de-DE 1.234,50 € fr-FR 1 234,50 € ja-JP ¥1,235

docs.title: Number Formatting
docs.text:
Thousand separators and decimal points vary by culture:

Culture {{ 1234567.89 \| format_number: "N2" }} en-US 1,234,567.89 de-DE 1.234.567,89 fr-FR 1 234 567,89

docs.title: Date Formatting
docs.text:
Date formats respect cultural conventions:

Culture {{ date \| date: "%x" }} (short date) en-US 01/15/24 en-GB 15/01/24 de-DE 15.01.24

Note

For consistent date output across cultures, use explicit format strings like "%Y-%m-%d" instead of locale-dependent formats like "%x".

docs.title: Common Cultures
docs.text: Code Language/Region Currency en-US English (United States) $ USD en-GB English (United Kingdom) £ GBP en-AU English (Australia) $ AUD en-CA English (Canada) $ CAD de-DE German (Germany) € EUR fr-FR French (France) € EUR es-ES Spanish (Spain) € EUR it-IT Italian (Italy) € EUR nl-NL Dutch (Netherlands) € EUR pt-BR Portuguese (Brazil) R$ BRL ja-JP Japanese (Japan) ¥ JPY zh-CN Chinese (China) ¥ CNY

docs.title: Multi-Currency Invoice
docs.text:
{% assign culture = customer.country | default: "en-US" %}
<!-- Culture set via API based on customer country -->

<table>
    {% for item in invoice.lines %}
    <tr>
        <td>{{ item.description }}</td>
        <td>{{ item.quantity }}</td>
        <td>{{ item.unitPrice | format_number: "C" }}</td>
        <td>{{ item.total | format_number: "C" }}</td>
    </tr>
    {% endfor %}
</table>

<p class="total">
    <strong>Total:</strong> {{ invoice.total | format_number: "C" }}
</p>

docs.title: Explicit Currency Symbol
docs.text:
If you need a specific currency regardless of culture:

<!-- Always show USD -->
${{ price | format_number: "N2" }}

<!-- Always show EUR -->
€{{ price | format_number: "N2" }}

<!-- Always show GBP -->
£{{ price | format_number: "N2" }}

docs.title: Regional Number Display
docs.text:
<!-- Using culture-aware formatting -->
<p>Population: {{ stats.population | format_number: "N0" }}</p>
<!-- en-US: 1,234,567 -->
<!-- de-DE: 1.234.567 -->

docs.title: Content Blocks and Culture
docs.text:
Content blocks inherit the culture from the parent template context:

<!-- Main template (culture: de-DE) -->
{{ contentBlock("cb_pricing", "price1", "product") }}

<!-- Content block will format as de-DE -->
<p>{{ price | format_number: "C" }}</p>
<!-- Output: 99,99 € -->

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Set culture at render time for dynamic multi-region support
  2. Use explicit formats for dates when consistency matters
  3. Test with multiple cultures if your templates serve international users
  4. Consider right-to-left cultures if supporting Arabic, Hebrew, etc.

docs.title: Wrong Currency Symbol
docs.text:
• Verify the culture code is correct
  • Check that cultureName is being passed in the API request
  • Default is typically en-US if not specified

docs.title: Numbers Not Formatting
docs.text:
• Ensure the value is a number, not a string
  • Use | to_number to convert strings first

docs.title: Unexpected Decimal Separator
docs.text:
• This is correct for the culture (e.g., comma in European cultures)
  • Use explicit format if you need consistent output: | format_number: "F2"

docs.text:

  • REST API - Setting culture in API requests
  • .NET Culture Codes - Full list of supported cultures

docs.title: Page Placeholders
docs.text: Page placeholders insert dynamic page information into PDF headers and footers. These are processed during PDF generation, not during Liquid templating.

docs.title: Available Placeholders
docs.text: Placeholder Description Example Output {{tt_pageNumber}} Current page number 1, 2, 3... {{tt_totalPages}} Total number of pages 5 {{tt_date}} Current date (browser locale date)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Page placeholders work only in PDF headers and footers. They're replaced at PDF render time by the browser engine.

docs.title: Adding to Header/Footer
docs.text:
In your template settings, add placeholders to your header or footer HTML:

Footer example: 

<div style="text-align: center; font-size: 10px; color: #666;">
    Page {{tt_pageNumber}} of {{tt_totalPages}}
</div>

Header example: 

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 9px;">
    <span>{{tt_date}}</span>
    <span>Confidential Document</span>
    <span>Page {{tt_pageNumber}}</span>
</div>

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Page placeholders are converted to special CSS class spans that the PDF renderer (Chromium) populates:

Placeholder Becomes {{tt_date}} <span class="date"></span> {{tt_pageNumber}} <span class="pageNumber"></span> {{tt_totalPages}} <span class="totalPages"></span>

The browser engine fills these spans with the actual values during PDF generation.

docs.title: Complete Footer Example
docs.text:
<div style="
    width: 100%;
    font-size: 9px;
    color: #888;
    padding: 10px 20px;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    border-top: 1px solid #eee;
">
    <span>Generated: {{tt_date}}</span>
    <span>{{companyName}}</span>
    <span>Page {{tt_pageNumber}} of {{tt_totalPages}}</span>
</div>

Mixing with Liquid Variables

You can use both page placeholders and Liquid variables in headers/footers. In the example above, {{companyName}} is a Liquid variable from your JSON data, while {{tt_pageNumber}} is a page placeholder.

docs.title: Centered Page Numbers
docs.text:
<div style="text-align: center; font-size: 10px;">
    - {{tt_pageNumber}} -
</div>

docs.title: Right-Aligned with Total
docs.text:
<div style="text-align: right; font-size: 9px; padding-right: 20px;">
    {{tt_pageNumber}} / {{tt_totalPages}}
</div>

docs.title: Conditional First Page
docs.text:
To hide page numbers on the first page, use CSS:

<style>
    @page:first {
        @bottom-center { content: none; }
    }
</style>
<div style="text-align: center;">
    Page {{tt_pageNumber}}
</div>

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Page placeholders only work in PDF output (not images or text)
  • They must be in the header or footer section of your template settings
  • They cannot be used with Liquid logic (e.g., {% if tt_pageNumber == 1 %} won't work)
  • The {{tt_date}} format depends on the browser's locale settings

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• PDF Generation - PDF-specific settings
  • Template Settings - Configuring headers and footers

docs.title: Template Themes
docs.text:
Themes allow you to share styling with all your templates and content blocks, reducing duplication and simplifying your template management.

Themes can be found in the Template sub menu. As shown above.

You can either Create a theme from scratch or upload a css file.

When you create or upload a new theme, it will get a card. The card has three buttons.

Button Description Delete Permanently remove the theme Edit Takes you to the theme editor, this is an in browser css editor. Default or Clear When you enable themes for a template. It will be the default theme that is applied.

Note

Although only being able to apply the default theme gives some limitation, this is a beta feature so there are some limitations while we gather feedback from customers.

docs.title: How themes work
docs.text:
On templates you want to apply your default theme to, go to template settings and enable themes. This will update the editor and apply the theme during generation.

When a theme is applied to a template, it will be applied to all components within that template during generations.

When editing a content block, you will need to go to the settings and toggle "Load theme" so the editor loads the same theme and the template.

docs.title: Working with Variables
docs.text: Variables let you create templates that generate personalized documents. Instead of hardcoding values, you use placeholders that get replaced with real data at render time.

docs.title: The Basics
docs.text:
Variables use double curly braces: {{variableName}}

When you render a template, you send JSON data. TemplateTo replaces each variable with the corresponding value from your data.

Template: 

Hello, {{name}}!

Data: 

{
  "name": "Alice"
}

Result: 

Hello, Alice!

docs.title: Adding Test Data
docs.text:
In the template editor, paste your JSON into the Template Data panel to test your template.

Sample JSON Data 
{
  "customerInvoice": {
    "name": "Lynx",
    "total": "123",
    "lines": [
      { "sku": "qwe123", "qnt": "2", "name": "Fragrance", "total": "82" },
      { "sku": "qwe124", "qnt": "1", "name": "Fragrance Bold", "total": "41" }
    ],
    "date": "15/11/23"
  },
  "email": "david@templateto.com",
  "country": "UK"
}

For simple key-value data, use the Create button to add variables without writing JSON manually.

docs.title: From the Editor
docs.text: Use the variable dropdown to insert variables without typing:

docs.title: By Typing
docs.text:
Type the variable name directly in your HTML:

<p>Customer: {{customerInvoice.name}}</p>
<p>Email: {{email}}</p>

docs.title: Accessing Nested Data
docs.text:
Use dot notation to access nested properties:

<!-- Access nested object properties -->
{{customerInvoice.name}}
{{customerInvoice.total}}
{{customerInvoice.date}}

For more complex data access patterns including arrays, see Data Binding.

docs.title: Liquid Templating
docs.text:
TemplateTo uses the Liquid templating engine. This gives you:

  • Variables: {{variable}}
  • Logic: {% if condition %}...{% endif %}
  • Loops: {% for item in collection %}...{% endfor %}
  • Filters: {{value | filter}}

See Liquid Reference for complete syntax documentation.

docs.title: Computed Variables
docs.text:
For complex transformations, create Liquid Variables in the editor:

  1. Navigate to the Data tab in the editor
  2. Give your variable a name
  3. Write your Liquid expression

Variable Order

If one variable uses another, define the dependency first. Variables are processed in order.

Example: Create a computed variable called formattedDate: 

{{ customerInvoice.date | parse_date | date: "%e %B %Y" }}

Then use it in your template: 

<p>Invoice Date: {{formattedDate}}</p>

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Data Binding - Learn about arrays, nested access, and JSON patterns
  • Filters & Tags - Format dates, numbers, and more
  • Liquid Reference - Complete Liquid syntax guide

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: TemplateTo provides special functions that extend Liquid's capabilities for document generation.

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text: Function Purpose Example repeat() Iterate with JSONPath {{ repeat("$.items[*]", "...", "...") }} contentBlock() Embed reusable blocks {{ contentBlock("cb_123", "comp1", "All") }} qrCode() Generate QR codes {{ qrCode(url) }} barcode() Generate barcodes {{ barcode(code, "CODE128") }} isArray() Check if value is array {% if isArray(items) %}

docs.title: Function Syntax
docs.text:
Functions use Liquid's output syntax with parentheses:

{{ functionName(argument1, argument2) }}

Functions can also be used in control flow:

{% if isArray(data) %}
    {% for item in data %}...{% endfor %}
{% endif %}

docs.title: repeat() vs for loops
docs.text:
Use standard {% for %} loops when: - Iterating over a simple array - You need full Liquid control flow

Use repeat() when: - You need JSONPath filtering - The array is deeply nested - You want to filter items with JSONPath expressions

docs.title: contentBlock() for reusability
docs.text: Use contentBlock() when: - Multiple templates share the same component - You want centralized styling/content updates - Building modular document systems

docs.title: qrCode() and barcode()
docs.text: Use these when: - Generating trackable documents - Creating shipping labels - Adding scannable links or references

docs.title: Functions in Detail
docs.text:
• repeat()

    JSONPath-based iteration for advanced data filtering

    Learn more

  • contentBlock()

    Embed reusable content blocks with data scoping

    Learn more

  • qrCode() & barcode()

    Generate QR codes and barcodes inline

    Learn more

  • Utilities

    Helper functions like isArray()

    Learn more

docs.title: Combining Functions
docs.text:
Functions can be combined with standard Liquid:

{% if showQRCode %}
    {{ qrCode(trackingUrl, "#000", "#fff", 10, 150, 150) }}
{% endif %}

{% if isArray(order.lines) %}
    {{ repeat("$.order.lines[*]", "<tr><td>{{name}}</td></tr>", "<table>_</table>") }}
{% else %}
    <p>Single item: {{ order.lines.name }}</p>
{% endif %}

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Liquid Reference - Standard Liquid syntax
  • Filters & Tags - TemplateTo filters and tags
  • Data Binding - Working with JSON data

docs.title: contentBlock() Function
docs.text: The contentBlock() function embeds reusable content blocks into your templates. Content blocks are standalone HTML/CSS components that can be shared across multiple templates.

docs.title: Why Use Content Blocks?
docs.text:
• Reusability: Define a component once, use it in many templates
  • Consistency: Update the block, and all templates using it get the changes
  • Data Scoping: Pass specific data subsets to each block
  • Modular Design: Build complex documents from smaller, testable pieces

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
{{ contentBlock(blockId, componentId, dataScope, customData) }}
Parameter Type Required Description blockId string Yes The content block ID (e.g., "cb_abc123") componentId string Yes Unique ID for this instance (for CSS scoping) dataScope string Yes Data to pass: "All", "Custom", or a JSON path customData string No Custom JSON data (when dataScope is "Custom")

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
Content Block HTML (defined separately): 

<div class="product-card">
    <h3>{{ name }}</h3>
    <p class="price">{{ price | format_number: "C" }}</p>
</div>

Template using the block: 

{{ contentBlock("cb_product123", "product1", "products[0]") }}

docs.title: "All" - Full Data Access
docs.text:
Pass all template data to the block:

{{ contentBlock("cb_header", "header1", "All") }}

The block receives the entire JSON object and can access any property.

docs.title: JSON Path - Specific Data
docs.text:
Pass a specific portion of your data:

<!-- Pass the customer object -->
{{ contentBlock("cb_address", "billTo", "customer.billingAddress") }}

<!-- Pass a specific array item -->
{{ contentBlock("cb_product", "prod1", "order.items[0]") }}

JSON: 

{
  "customer": {
    "billingAddress": {
      "street": "123 Main St",
      "city": "London"
    }
  }
}

Content Block receives: 

{
  "street": "123 Main St",
  "city": "London"
}

docs.title: "Custom" - Dynamic Data
docs.text:
Build custom data dynamically:

{{ contentBlock("cb_summary", "summary1", "Custom", '{"total": "{{order.total}}", "count": "{{order.items.size}}"}') }}

The custom data JSON is processed through Liquid first, then passed to the block.

docs.title: Component ID (CSS Scoping)
docs.text:
The componentId ensures CSS from one block doesn't affect others:

<!-- Two instances of the same block with different data -->
{{ contentBlock("cb_card", "card1", "products[0]") }}
{{ contentBlock("cb_card", "card2", "products[1]") }}

CSS in the content block is automatically scoped:

/* In content block */
.card { background: white; }

/* Rendered as */
#card1 .card { background: white; }
#card2 .card { background: white; }

docs.title: Manual Iteration
docs.text:
{% for item in order.items %}
    {{ contentBlock("cb_lineItem", "line" | append: forloop.index, "order.items[" | append: forloop.index0 | append: "]") }}
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Array as Data Scope
docs.text:
When you pass an array path, the block renders once per item:

{{ contentBlock("cb_row", "rows", "order.items") }}

If order.items is an array with 3 items, the block renders 3 times.

docs.title: Debugging with tt_dumpData
docs.text:
Inside a content block, use {{tt_dumpData}} to see what data is available:

Content Block HTML: 

<div class="debug">
    <h4>Available Data:</h4>
    {{tt_dumpData}}
</div>
<div class="content">
    <h3>{{ name }}</h3>
</div>

This renders the scoped data as prettified JSON in a <pre> tag.

Warning

Remove {{tt_dumpData}} before production use. It's only for debugging.

docs.title: Invoice Header Block
docs.text:
Content Block (cb_invoiceHeader): 

<div class="invoice-header">
    <div class="company">
        <img src="{{ company.logo }}" alt="{{ company.name }}">
        <h1>{{ company.name }}</h1>
    </div>
    <div class="invoice-details">
        <p><strong>Invoice:</strong> {{ invoice.number }}</p>
        <p><strong>Date:</strong> {{ invoice.date | parse_date | date: "%B %d, %Y" }}</p>
    </div>
</div>

Template: 

{{ contentBlock("cb_invoiceHeader", "header", "All") }}

docs.title: Address Block (Reused for Bill To / Ship To)
docs.text:
Content Block (cb_address): 

<div class="address">
    <p><strong>{{ name }}</strong></p>
    <p>{{ street }}</p>
    <p>{{ city }}, {{ state }} {{ zip }}</p>
    <p>{{ country }}</p>
</div>

Template: 

<div class="addresses">
    <div class="bill-to">
        <h3>Bill To:</h3>
        {{ contentBlock("cb_address", "billTo", "customer.billing") }}
    </div>
    <div class="ship-to">
        <h3>Ship To:</h3>
        {{ contentBlock("cb_address", "shipTo", "customer.shipping") }}
    </div>
</div>

docs.title: Product Card Grid
docs.text:
Content Block (cb_productCard): 

<div class="card">
    <img src="{{ image }}" alt="{{ name }}">
    <h4>{{ name }}</h4>
    <p class="price">{{ price | format_number: "C" }}</p>
    {% if onSale %}
        <span class="badge">Sale!</span>
    {% endif %}
</div>

Template: 

<div class="product-grid">
    {% for product in products %}
        {{ contentBlock("cb_productCard", "prod" | append: forloop.index, "products[" | append: forloop.index0 | append: "]") }}
    {% endfor %}
</div>

docs.title: Creating Content Blocks
docs.text:
Content blocks are created in the TemplateTo UI:

  1. Go to Templates > Content Blocks
  2. Click Create Content Block
  3. Add your HTML and CSS
  4. Note the block ID (shown in the URL or settings)

The block ID format is typically cb_ followed by an identifier.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Keep blocks focused: One component per block
  2. Use meaningful componentIds: "header", "footer", "productCard1" instead of "a", "b"
  3. Document data requirements: Note what properties the block expects
  4. Test with tt_dumpData: Verify the block receives expected data
  5. Consider CSS conflicts: Use the component scoping feature

docs.title: Block Not Rendering
docs.text:
• Verify the block ID is correct
  • Check that the block exists in your account
  • Ensure the block is associated with your template

docs.title: Wrong Data in Block
docs.text:
• Use {{tt_dumpData}} to see what data the block receives
  • Check your data scope path
  • Verify JSON paths are correct (case-sensitive)

docs.title: CSS Conflicts
docs.text:
• Ensure each instance has a unique componentId
  • Avoid body selectors in block CSS (they're automatically removed)

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Functions Overview - All available functions
  • Themes - Sharing CSS across templates
  • Debugging - Troubleshooting tips

docs.title: QR Codes & Barcodes
docs.text: Generate QR codes and barcodes directly in your templates using the qrCode() and barcode() functions.

docs.title: qrCode()
docs.text: Generate QR codes that can encode URLs, text, or any string data.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
{{ qrCode(content, foreground, background, margin, width, height) }}
Parameter Type Default Description content string (required) Data to encode (URL, text, etc.) foreground string #000000 Foreground color (hex) background string #ffffff Background color (hex) margin number 0 Margin around code (pixels) width number 136 Width (pixels) height number 136 Height (pixels)

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text: {{ qrCode("https://example.com") }}

docs.title: With Styling
docs.text: {{ qrCode("https://example.com", "#1a1a1a", "#f5f5f5", 10, 200, 200) }}

docs.title: Using Variables
docs.text:
{{ qrCode(order.trackingUrl) }}

{{ qrCode(invoice.paymentLink, "#000", "#fff", 5, 150, 150) }}

docs.title: Dynamic Content
docs.text:
You can use Liquid variables inside the content:

{{ qrCode("https://myapp.com/order/{{order.id}}") }}

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The qrCode() function outputs an inline SVG wrapped in a span:

<span style="padding: 10px; background: #FFF; display: inline-block;">
    <svg>...</svg>
</span>

docs.title: barcode()
docs.text: Generate various barcode formats for product labels, shipping, and inventory.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
{{ barcode(content, format, foreground, background, fontSize, margin, width, height, noText) }}
Parameter Type Default Description content string (required) Data to encode format string (required) Barcode format (see below) foreground string #000000 Foreground color (hex) background string #ffffff Background color (hex) fontSize number 10 Text font size margin number 0 Margin around code (pixels) width number 136 Width (pixels) height number 136 Height (pixels) noText boolean false Hide the text below barcode

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text: Format Description Use Case CODE128 High-density alphanumeric General purpose, shipping CODE39 Alphanumeric Industrial, government EAN13 13-digit numeric Retail products (Europe) EAN8 8-digit numeric Small retail products UPCA 12-digit numeric Retail products (US) UPCE 6-digit numeric Small retail products (US) ITF Interleaved 2 of 5 Shipping, warehouse QR_CODE QR Code Use qrCode() instead

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text: {{ barcode("ABC123456", "CODE128") }}

docs.title: Product Labels
docs.text: {{ barcode(product.sku, "CODE128", "#000", "#fff", 12, 5, 200, 80) }}

docs.title: Shipping Labels
docs.text: {{ barcode(shipment.trackingNumber, "CODE128", "#000", "#fff", 10, 10, 300, 100) }}

docs.title: Without Text
docs.text: {{ barcode(product.upc, "UPCA", "#000", "#fff", 10, 0, 200, 60, true) }}

docs.title: Using Variables
docs.text:
{{ barcode(order.id, "CODE128") }}
{{ barcode(product.ean, "EAN13", "#000", "#fff", 8, 5, 150, 70) }}

docs.title: Invoice with Payment QR Code
docs.text:
<div class="invoice">
    <h1>Invoice #{{ invoice.number }}</h1>

    <div class="payment-section">
        <h3>Scan to Pay</h3>
        {{ qrCode(invoice.paymentUrl, "#000", "#fff", 10, 150, 150) }}
        <p class="small">Or visit: {{ invoice.paymentUrl }}</p>
    </div>
</div>

docs.title: Shipping Label
docs.text:
<div class="shipping-label">
    <div class="address">
        <strong>{{ shipment.recipient.name }}</strong><br>
        {{ shipment.recipient.address }}<br>

docs.title: repeat() Function
docs.text: The repeat() function provides powerful JSONPath-based iteration, allowing you to filter and iterate over arrays using JSONPath expressions.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
{{ repeat(jsonPath, itemTemplate, wrapperTemplate) }}
Parameter Type Required Description jsonPath string Yes JSONPath expression to select items itemTemplate string Yes Template rendered for each item wrapperTemplate string No Wrapper around all items (use _ as placeholder)

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
JSON Data: 

{
  "products": [
    { "name": "Widget", "price": 10 },
    { "name": "Gadget", "price": 25 },
    { "name": "Gizmo", "price": 15 }
  ]
}

Template: 

{{ repeat("$.products[*]", "<li>{{name}} - ${{price}}</li>", "<ul>_</ul>") }}

Output: 

<ul>
    <li>Widget - $10</li>
    <li>Gadget - $25</li>
    <li>Gizmo - $15</li>
</ul>

docs.title: JSONPath Syntax
docs.text:
JSONPath is like XPath for JSON. Here are common patterns:

Expression Description $.property Root property $.obj.nested Nested property $.array[*] All array items $.array[0] First array item $.array[-1] Last array item $.array[0:3] Items 0, 1, 2 $..property Recursive descent (find all) $.array[?(@.active)] Filter: where active is truthy $.array[?(@.price > 10)] Filter: where price > 10

docs.title: Filter by Property Value
docs.text:
<!-- Only active items -->
{{ repeat("$.items[?(@.active == true)]", "<li>{{name}}</li>", "<ul>_</ul>") }}

<!-- Items with status 'pending' -->
{{ repeat("$.orders[?(@.status == 'pending')]", "<tr><td>{{id}}</td></tr>", "<table>_</table>") }}

docs.title: Filter by Numeric Comparison
docs.text:
<!-- Products over $50 -->
{{ repeat("$.products[?(@.price > 50)]", "<div>{{name}}: ${{price}}</div>", "") }}

<!-- Orders with quantity >= 10 -->
{{ repeat("$.orders[?(@.qty >= 10)]", "{{id}}, ", "") }}

docs.title: Combine Filters
docs.text:
<!-- Active products under $100 -->
{{ repeat("$.products[?(@.active && @.price < 100)]", "<li>{{name}}</li>", "<ul>_</ul>") }}

docs.title: Item Template Context
docs.text:
Inside the item template, you can access:

  • Direct properties: {{propertyName}}
  • The current item as _: {{_}}
  • Nested properties: {{nested.property}}

Example with nested data:

{
  "orders": [
    {
      "id": "ORD-001",
      "customer": { "name": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com" },
      "total": 150
    }
  ]
}

{{ repeat("$.orders[*]",
    "<div class='order'>
        <h3>Order {{id}}</h3>
        <p>Customer: {{customer.name}}</p>
        <p>Total: ${{total}}</p>
    </div>",
    "")
}}

docs.title: Wrapper Template
docs.text:
The third parameter wraps all rendered items. Use _ as a placeholder for the content.

Without wrapper: 

{{ repeat("$.items[*]", "<li>{{name}}</li>", "") }}
<!-- Output: <li>A</li><li>B</li><li>C</li> -->

With wrapper: 

{{ repeat("$.items[*]", "<li>{{name}}</li>", "<ul class='my-list'>_</ul>") }}
<!-- Output: <ul class='my-list'><li>A</li><li>B</li><li>C</li></ul> -->

docs.title: Building a Table
docs.text:
{{ repeat("$.invoice.lines[*]",
    "<tr>
        <td>{{description}}</td>
        <td>{{quantity}}</td>
        <td>${{unitPrice}}</td>
        <td>${{total}}</td>
    </tr>",
    "<table class='invoice-lines'>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Description</th>
                <th>Qty</th>
                <th>Unit Price</th>
                <th>Total</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>_</tbody>
    </table>")
}}

docs.title: Category Listing
docs.text:
{
  "categories": [
    {
      "name": "Electronics",
      "products": [
        { "name": "Phone", "inStock": true },
        { "name": "Laptop", "inStock": false }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

{% for category in categories %}
<h2>{{ category.name }}</h2>
{{ repeat("$.categories[" | append: forloop.index0 | append: "].products[?(@.inStock == true)]",
    "<li>{{name}} - In Stock</li>",
    "<ul>_</ul>") }}
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Badge/Tag List
docs.text:
{{ repeat("$.tags[*]",
    "<span class='badge'>{{_}}</span>",
    "<div class='tags'>_</div>") }}

docs.title: Comparison with for Loops
docs.text:
Feature {% for %} repeat() Simple iteration Yes Yes JSONPath filtering No Yes Loop variables (index, first, last) Yes No Nested loops Yes Limited Wrapper syntax Manual Built-in Liquid logic inside Full Limited

Use {% for %} when: - You need forloop.index, forloop.first, etc. - You need complex Liquid logic inside the loop - The data structure is simple

Use repeat() when: - You need to filter items with JSONPath - You want concise table/list generation - The array is deeply nested

docs.title: No output
docs.text:
• Verify the JSONPath is correct using a JSONPath tester
  • Check that the data matches your filter criteria
  • Ensure the JSON property names are correct (case-sensitive)

docs.title: Partial output
docs.text:
• JSONPath filters might be excluding items
  • Check filter conditions: @.property == 'value' (use single quotes for strings)

docs.title: HTML entities appearing
docs.text: If you see < instead of <, the output is being double-escaped. This shouldn't normally happen with repeat().

docs.title: isArray()
docs.text: Checks whether a value is an array. Returns true or false.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
{% if isArray(value) %}
    ...
{% endif %}

docs.title: Why Use isArray()?
docs.text:
When your data structure might be either a single object or an array, isArray() lets you handle both cases:

Data might be: 

// Single item
{ "order": { "name": "Widget", "qty": 1 } }

// Or multiple items
{ "order": [
    { "name": "Widget", "qty": 1 },
    { "name": "Gadget", "qty": 2 }
] }

Template: 

{% if isArray(order) %}
    {% for item in order %}
        <div>{{ item.name }}: {{ item.qty }}</div>
    {% endfor %}
{% else %}
    <div>{{ order.name }}: {{ order.qty }}</div>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Dynamic List vs Single Item
docs.text:
{% if isArray(recipients) %}
    <h3>Recipients:</h3>
    <ul>
        {% for person in recipients %}
            <li>{{ person.name }} <{{ person.email }}></li>
        {% endfor %}
    </ul>
{% else %}
    <h3>Recipient:</h3>
    <p>{{ recipients.name }} <{{ recipients.email }}></p>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Conditional Table Rendering
docs.text:
{% if isArray(data.items) and data.items.size > 0 %}
    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Item</th><th>Price</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            {% for item in data.items %}
            <tr>
                <td>{{ item.name }}</td>
                <td>{{ item.price | format_number: "C" }}</td>
            </tr>
            {% endfor %}
        </tbody>
    </table>
{% elsif data.items %}
    <p>Single item: {{ data.items.name }}</p>
{% else %}
    <p>No items.</p>
{% endif %}

docs.title: API Response Handling
docs.text:
APIs sometimes return different structures based on result count:

{% if isArray(response.results) %}
    Found {{ response.results.size }} results
{% else %}
    Single result: {{ response.results.title }}
{% endif %}

docs.title: Combining with Other Checks
docs.text:
{% if items and isArray(items) and items.size > 0 %}
    <!-- Safe to iterate -->
    {% for item in items %}...{% endfor %}
{% endif %}

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
isArray() checks the underlying Fluid value type:

Value isArray() returns [] (empty array) true [1, 2, 3] true [{...}, {...}] true {} (object) false "string" false 123 false null false

docs.title: "isArray not found" error
docs.text:
Ensure you're using the function in a conditional, not as output:

<!-- Wrong -->
{{ isArray(items) }}

<!-- Right -->
{% if isArray(items) %}...{% endif %}

docs.title: Always returns false
docs.text:
• Check that the property path is correct
  • The property might not exist (returns false for undefined)
  • Use {{ items | json }} to inspect the actual structure

docs.title: Type Checking Alternatives
docs.text:
For simple checks, you can also use Liquid's built-in properties:

<!-- Check if has items -->
{% if items.size > 0 %}...{% endif %}

<!-- Check if exists and not blank -->
{% if items != blank %}...{% endif %}

<!-- Check first item exists -->
{% if items.first %}...{% endif %}

However, these don't distinguish between an array and an object with a size property.

docs.title: Conditional Content
docs.text: Show or hide sections of your template based on data values. These patterns help create flexible templates that adapt to different scenarios.

docs.title: Basic If Statement
docs.text:
Show content only when a condition is true:

{% if customer.isPremium %}
    <div class="premium-badge">Premium Member</div>
{% endif %}

docs.title: If/Else
docs.text:
Handle both cases:

{% if order.shipped %}
    <p>Your order has shipped!</p>
{% else %}
    <p>Your order is being processed.</p>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Multiple Conditions (elsif)
docs.text:
Check several possibilities:

{% if order.status == "delivered" %}
    <span class="status delivered">Delivered</span>
{% elsif order.status == "shipped" %}
    <span class="status shipped">In Transit</span>
{% elsif order.status == "processing" %}
    <span class="status processing">Processing</span>
{% else %}
    <span class="status pending">Pending</span>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Exists and Not Empty
docs.text:
<!-- Check if property exists and has a value -->
{% if customer.phone %}
    <p>Phone: {{ customer.phone }}</p>
{% endif %}

<!-- Check for non-blank string -->
{% if customer.notes != blank %}
    <div class="notes">{{ customer.notes }}</div>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Checking for Null/Empty
docs.text:
{% if address == nil %}
    <p>No address on file</p>
{% endif %}

{% if items == empty %}
    <p>No items in cart</p>
{% endif %}

{% if items.size == 0 %}
    <p>Your cart is empty</p>
{% endif %}

docs.text:
{% if country == "UK" %}

{% endif %}

{% if quantity == 1 %}
    <span>item</span>
{% else %}
    <span>items</span>
{% endif %}

{% endif %}

{% if stock <= 5 %}
    <span class="low-stock">Only {{ stock }} left!</span>
{% endif %}

{% if age >= 18 %}
    <p>Adult content accessible</p>
{% endif %}

docs.title: And (both must be true)
docs.text:
{% if user.verified and user.active %}
    <span class="verified-badge">Verified User</span>
{% endif %}

{% if quantity > 0 and inStock %}
    <button>Add to Cart</button>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Or (either can be true)

{% if isAdmin or isModerator %}
    <a href="/admin">Admin Panel</a>
{% endif %}

{% if paymentMethod == "credit" or paymentMethod == "debit" %}

{% endif %}

docs.text:

{% endif %}

docs.text:

{% endif %}

{% if product.tags contains "sale" %}
    <span class="sale-badge">On Sale!</span>

The opposite of if:

{% unless order.paid %}
    <div class="payment-reminder">
        Payment is still pending.
    </div>
{% endunless %}

<!-- Equivalent to: -->
{% if order.paid == false %}
    ...
{% endif %}

For multiple specific values:

{% case shipping.method %}
    {% when "standard" %}

    {% when "express" %}

    {% when "overnight" %}

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Keep conditions simple - Complex logic is hard to debug
  2. Check for existence first - {% if obj %}{% if obj.property %}{% endif %}{% endif %}
  3. Use meaningful variable names - isPremium is clearer than p
  4. Consider default values - {{ value | default: "N/A" }}
  5. Document complex conditions - Add comments for future reference

docs.title: Tutorial: Building an Invoice Template
docs.text: This tutorial walks through creating a complete invoice template from scratch. You'll learn how to structure your data, display company and customer information, iterate over line items, and calculate totals.

docs.title: What We're Building
docs.text: A professional invoice with: - Company header - Customer billing details - Line items table - Subtotal, tax, and total - Payment information - Page numbers

docs.title: Step 1: Define Your Data Structure
docs.text:
Start by planning your JSON data. Here's a typical invoice structure:

{
  "company": {
    "name": "Acme Solutions Ltd",
    "address": "123 Business Park",
    "city": "London",
    "postcode": "EC1A 1BB",
    "phone": "+44 20 1234 5678",
    "email": "billing@acme.com",
    "vatNumber": "GB123456789"
  },
  "invoice": {
    "number": "INV-2024-001",
    "date": "15/01/24",
    "dueDate": "15/02/24",
    "poNumber": "PO-5678"
  },
  "customer": {
    "name": "Widget Corp",
    "contact": "Jane Smith",
    "address": "456 Client Street",
    "city": "Manchester",
    "postcode": "M1 1AA"
  },
  "items": [
    {
      "description": "Consulting Services",
      "quantity": 10,
      "unit": "hours",
      "unitPrice": 150.00,
      "total": 1500.00
    },
    {
      "description": "Software License",
      "quantity": 1,
      "unit": "license",
      "unitPrice": 499.00,
      "total": 499.00
    },
    {
      "description": "Support Package",
      "quantity": 1,
      "unit": "month",
      "unitPrice": 200.00,
      "total": 200.00
    }
  ],
  "subtotal": 2199.00,
  "taxRate": 20,
  "taxAmount": 439.80,
  "total": 2638.80,
  "notes": "Payment terms: Net 30 days",
  "bankDetails": {
    "name": "Acme Solutions Ltd",
    "bank": "Example Bank",
    "sortCode": "12-34-56",
    "accountNumber": "12345678"
  }
}

Paste this into the Template Data panel in the editor.

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Header
docs.text:
Start with the company information and invoice details:

<div class="invoice-header">
    <div class="company-info">
        <h1>{{ company.name }}</h1>
        <p>{{ company.address }}</p>
        <p>{{ company.city }}, {{ company.postcode }}</p>
        <p>{{ company.phone }}</p>
        <p>{{ company.email }}</p>
    </div>

    <div class="invoice-details">
        <h2>INVOICE</h2>
        <table>
            <tr>
                <td>Invoice No:</td>
                <td><strong>{{ invoice.number }}</strong></td>

docs.title: Iteration Patterns
docs.text: Common patterns for displaying array data as tables, lists, cards, and grids.

docs.title: Basic Table
docs.text:
The most common pattern - display array data in a table:

Data: 

{
  "products": [
    { "name": "Widget", "sku": "WGT-001", "price": 29.99, "stock": 150 },
    { "name": "Gadget", "sku": "GDG-002", "price": 49.99, "stock": 75 },
    { "name": "Gizmo", "sku": "GZM-003", "price": 19.99, "stock": 200 }
  ]
}

Template: 

<table>
    <thead>
        <tr>
            <th>SKU</th>
            <th>Product</th>
            <th>Price</th>
            <th>Stock</th>
        </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        {% for product in products %}
        <tr>
            <td>{{ product.sku }}</td>
            <td>{{ product.name }}</td>
            <td>{{ product.price | format_number: "C" }}</td>
            <td>{{ product.stock }}</td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
    </tbody>
</table>

docs.title: Table with Row Numbers
docs.text:
Add row numbers using forloop.index:

<tbody>
    {% for item in items %}
    <tr>
        <td>{{ forloop.index }}</td>
        <td>{{ item.name }}</td>
        <td>{{ item.value }}</td>
    </tr>
    {% endfor %}
</tbody>

docs.title: Table with Alternating Rows
docs.text:
Style odd/even rows differently:

{% for item in items %}
<tr class="{% if forloop.index | modulo: 2 == 0 %}even{% else %}odd{% endif %}">
    <td>{{ item.name }}</td>
</tr>
{% endfor %}

CSS: 

tr.odd { background: #f9f9f9; }
tr.even { background: #ffffff; }

docs.title: Table with Row Totals
docs.text:
Calculate and display totals per row:

{% for line in order.lines %}
<tr>
    <td>{{ line.description }}</td>
    <td>{{ line.quantity }}</td>
    <td>{{ line.unitPrice | format_number: "C" }}</td>
    <td>{{ line.quantity | times: line.unitPrice | format_number: "C" }}</td>
</tr>
{% endfor %}

docs.text:

<ul>
    {% for item in items %}
    <li>{{ item.name }}</li>

<ol>
    {% for step in steps %}

docs.text:
Display items as cards in a flexible grid:

Template: 

<div class="card-grid">
    {% for product in products %}

        <p class="price">{{ product.price | format_number: "C" }}</p>

    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
    gap: 20px;
}

.card {
    border: 1px solid #ddd;
    padding: 15px;
    border-radius: 8px;
}

docs.title: Two-Column Layout
docs.text:
Split items into two columns:

<div class="two-columns">
    <div class="column">
        {% for item in items limit: items.size | divided_by: 2 %}
        <p>{{ item.name }}</p>
        {% endfor %}
    </div>
    <div class="column">
        {% for item in items offset: items.size | divided_by: 2 %}
        <p>{{ item.name }}</p>
        {% endfor %}
    </div>
</div>

docs.title: Nested Loops
docs.text:
Iterate over nested arrays:

Data: 

{
  "categories": [
    {
      "name": "Electronics",
      "items": [
        { "name": "Phone", "price": 699 },
        { "name": "Laptop", "price": 1299 }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Books",
      "items": [
        { "name": "Novel", "price": 15 },
        { "name": "Textbook", "price": 85 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Template: 

{% for category in categories %}
<h2>{{ category.name }}</h2>
<ul>
    {% for item in category.items %}
    <li>{{ item.name }} - {{ item.price | format_number: "C" }}</li>
    {% endfor %}
</ul>
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Grouped Items
docs.text:
Group items by a property:

Data: 

{
  "orders": [
    { "status": "pending", "id": "001", "total": 150 },
    { "status": "shipped", "id": "002", "total": 200 },
    { "status": "pending", "id": "003", "total": 75 },
    { "status": "delivered", "id": "004", "total": 300 }
  ]
}

Using repeat() with JSONPath filtering: 

<h3>Pending Orders</h3>
{{ repeat("$.orders[?(@.status=='pending')]",
    "<p>Order {{id}}: {{total | format_number: 'C'}}</p>",
    "") }}

<h3>Shipped Orders</h3>
{{ repeat("$.orders[?(@.status=='shipped')]",
    "<p>Order {{id}}: {{total | format_number: 'C'}}</p>",
    "") }}

docs.title: Empty State
docs.text:
Handle empty arrays gracefully:

{% for item in items %}
<div class="item">{{ item.name }}</div>
{% else %}
<div class="empty-state">
    <p>No items to display.</p>
</div>
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Limited Display
docs.text:
Show only a subset of items:

<!-- First 5 items -->
<h3>Top 5 Products</h3>
{% for product in products limit: 5 %}
<p>{{ product.name }}</p>
{% endfor %}

<!-- Show "and X more" -->
{% if products.size > 5 %}
<p class="more">and {{ products.size | minus: 5 }} more...</p>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Pagination Pattern
docs.text:
For multi-page documents with many items:

{% for item in items %}
<div class="item">
    {{ item.name }}
</div>

<!-- Page break every 10 items -->
{% assign remainder = forloop.index | modulo: 10 %}
{% if remainder == 0 and forloop.last == false %}
<div style="page-break-after: always;"></div>
{% endif %}
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Summary Statistics
docs.text:
Show count and totals:

<p>Total items: {{ items.size }}</p>

{% assign total = 0 %}
{% for item in items %}
    {% assign total = total | plus: item.price %}
{% endfor %}
<p>Total value: {{ total | format_number: "C" }}</p>

docs.title: Conditional Row Styling
docs.text:
Highlight specific rows:

{% for order in orders %}
<tr class="{% if order.priority == 'high' %}highlight{% endif %} {% if order.overdue %}overdue{% endif %}">
    <td>{{ order.id }}</td>
    <td>{{ order.customer }}</td>
    <td>{{ order.total | format_number: "C" }}</td>
</tr>
{% endfor %}

CSS: 

tr.highlight { background: #fff3cd; }
tr.overdue { color: #dc3545; }

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text: TemplateTo can generate documents in multiple formats. Choose the right format for your use case.

docs.title: Available Formats
docs.text:
• PDF Generation

    Multi-page documents with headers, footers, and password protection

    PDF Guide

  • Image Generation

    PNG and JPEG images with clips, masks, and retina support

    Image Guide

  • Plain Text

    TXT output for emails, SMS, and data exports

    TXT Guide

docs.title: Format Comparison
docs.text: Feature PDF PNG JPEG TXT Multi-page Yes No No Yes Formatting Full Full Full None Transparency No Yes No N/A File size Medium Large Small Tiny Password protection Yes No No No Headers/footers Yes No No No Printable Yes Yes Yes Yes Web display Embed Native Native Pre-formatted

docs.title: PDF
docs.text:
Best for documents that need to be:

  • Printed or downloaded
  • Multi-page with consistent formatting
  • Password protected
  • Archived with exact layout preservation

Examples: Invoices, contracts, reports, certificates

docs.title: PNG
docs.text:
Best for images that need:

  • Transparency (logos, overlays)
  • Lossless quality
  • Sharp text and graphics

Examples: Social media graphics, logos, diagrams, Open Graph images

docs.title: JPEG
docs.text:
Best for images that need:

  • Smaller file sizes
  • Photographic content
  • Fast web loading

Examples: Thumbnails, email headers, photo-based graphics

docs.title: TXT
docs.text:
Best for content that needs:

  • Maximum compatibility
  • No formatting
  • Small file size
  • Easy parsing

Examples: Email body content, SMS messages, data exports, notifications

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
All formats are available through both sync and async APIs:

Format Sync Endpoint Async Endpoint PDF POST /render/pdf/{templateId} POST /render/async/pdf/{templateId} Image POST /render/image/{templateId} POST /render/async/image/{templateId} TXT POST /render/txt/{templateId} POST /render/async/txt/{templateId}

See the REST API Reference for complete documentation.

docs.title: Image Generation
docs.text: Render your templates as PNG or JPEG images. This is useful for social media graphics, thumbnails, email headers, and any web-displayable content.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Image output is ideal for:

  • Social media graphics (Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn)
  • Open Graph images for link previews
  • Email headers and signatures
  • Thumbnails and previews
  • Certificates and badges
  • Profile pictures and avatars

docs.title: PNG
docs.text:
• Transparency support - Create images with transparent backgrounds
  • Lossless compression - No quality loss
  • Best for - Graphics, logos, images with text, anything requiring transparency

docs.title: JPEG
docs.text:
• Smaller file sizes - Better compression for photographs
  • Adjustable quality - Trade quality for size
  • Best for - Photographs, images where transparency isn't needed

docs.title: Image Settings
docs.text:
When rendering images via the API, you can control these settings:

Setting Default Description format png Output format: png or jpeg width from template Image width in pixels height auto Image height in pixels (only when fullPage=false) quality 90 JPEG quality (0-100). Higher = better quality, larger file fullPage true Capture entire scrollable content scale 1 Device scale factor (use 2 for retina/high-DPI)

docs.title: Width and Height
docs.text:
By default, image width is derived from your template's page size setting. You can override this with the width parameter.

When fullPage=true (default), height is determined automatically based on content. Set fullPage=false to use a fixed height.

docs.title: Scale Factor
docs.text:
The scale parameter controls pixel density:

  • scale=1 - Standard resolution (1x)
  • scale=2 - Retina/high-DPI resolution (2x)

A 1200x630 image at scale=2 produces a 2400x1260 pixel image that displays sharply on retina screens.

docs.title: Full Page vs Fixed Height
docs.text:
Full Page (fullPage=true):

  • Captures all content regardless of length
  • Height adjusts automatically
  • Use for templates with variable content

Fixed Height (fullPage=false):

  • Captures exactly the viewport size
  • Set specific height parameter
  • Use for fixed-size outputs (social media dimensions)

docs.title: Clip Regions
docs.text: Extract specific portions of your rendered template using clip regions.

docs.title: Single Clip
docs.text:
Capture a rectangular region from the rendered content:

{
  "clipX": 0,
  "clipY": 0,
  "clipWidth": 800,
  "clipHeight": 400
}
Parameter Description clipX X coordinate (pixels from left edge) clipY Y coordinate (pixels from top edge) clipWidth Width of region to capture clipHeight Height of region to capture

docs.title: Multiple Clips
docs.text:
Extract multiple regions from a single render using the clips endpoint. This is efficient when you need several variations from the same template.

{
  "data": {
    "customerName": "Acme Corp"
  },
  "clips": [
    { "name": "header", "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1200, "height": 300 },
    { "name": "og-image", "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1200, "height": 630 },
    { "name": "thumbnail", "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 400, "height": 400 }
  ]
}

Use cases:

  • Generate multiple social media sizes from one design
  • Create both full image and thumbnail in one request
  • Extract header, body, and footer sections separately

docs.title: Circular Masks
docs.text:
Create circular (or elliptical) images with transparent backgrounds - perfect for avatars and profile pictures.

{
  "clipX": 0,
  "clipY": 0,
  "clipWidth": 200,
  "clipHeight": 200,
  "circular": true
}

When circular=true:

  • The clip region is masked to a circle (or ellipse if width ≠ height)
  • Output is automatically PNG to support transparency
  • Background outside the circle is transparent

Example use cases:

  • User avatars
  • Profile pictures
  • Round badges or icons

  -H "X-Api-Key: your-api-key" \

curl -X POST "https://api.templateto.com/render/image/tpl_abc123?scale=2&width=1200" \

  'https://api.templateto.com/render/image/tpl_abc123/clips',
  {

    },
    body: JSON.stringify({

      clips: [
        { name: 'instagram', x: 0, y: 0, width: 1080, height: 1080 },
        { name: 'twitter', x: 0, y: 0, width: 1200, height: 675 },
        { name: 'og', x: 0, y: 0, width: 1200, height: 630 }
      ]
    })
  }
);

// Response is a ZIP file (application/zip) containing:
//   instagram.png, twitter.png, og.png, manifest.json
const zip = await response.blob();

docs.title: PDF Generation
docs.text: TemplateTo generates high-quality PDF documents from your templates. This guide covers PDF-specific settings and features.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PDF output is ideal for:

  • Printable documents (invoices, contracts, reports)
  • Multi-page content with page breaks
  • Documents requiring headers and footers
  • Password-protected files
  • Official documents requiring consistent formatting

docs.title: PDF Settings
docs.text: Access PDF settings through the Template Settings panel in the editor.

docs.title: Paper Size
docs.text:
Choose from standard sizes or define custom dimensions:

Standard sizes:

  • A4 (210mm x 297mm) - Default
  • Letter (8.5" x 11")
  • Legal (8.5" x 14")
  • A3, A5, and more

Custom size: Select "Custom" and enter dimensions in millimeters.

docs.title: Orientation
docs.text:
• Portrait (default) - Taller than wide
  • Landscape - Wider than tall

docs.title: Print Background
docs.text: Enable to include background colors and images in the PDF. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: Margins
docs.text:
Set margins for top, bottom, left, and right edges.

Note

Headers and footers render within the margins. Ensure adequate margin space when using headers/footers.

docs.title: Headers and Footers
docs.text: Add consistent headers and footers to every page of your document.

docs.title: Enabling Headers/Footers
docs.text:
1. Open Template Settings
  2. Toggle "Display Header / Footer"
  3. Select content blocks for header and/or footer

docs.title: Using Content Blocks
docs.text:
Headers and footers use Content Blocks - reusable pieces of content you can share across templates.

Create content blocks at: Content Block Manager

docs.title: Page Numbers
docs.text:
Use Liquid variables in your header/footer content blocks:

  • {{page}} - Current page number
  • {{pages}} - Total page count

Example footer: Page {{page}} of {{pages}}

docs.title: Cover Page
docs.text:
Apply different settings to the first page of your document.

Cover page options let you:

  • Use different margins for page 1
  • Hide headers/footers on the cover
  • Apply different orientation

docs.title: Password Protection
docs.text: Secure your PDFs with password protection and permission controls.

docs.title: Enabling Protection
docs.text:
1. Open Template Settings
  2. Toggle "Password Protection"
  3. Configure options

docs.title: Protection Options
docs.text:
Option Description Password Password to open the document. Supports variables like {{customerPassword}} Permit Print Allow printing Permit Modify Allow editing document content Permit Extract Allow copying text and images Permit Annotations Allow adding comments and annotations

Dynamic Passwords

The password field accepts template variables. Use {{password}} and pass a unique password in your API request for per-document encryption.

docs.title: Page Breaks
docs.text: Control where new pages begin in your document.

docs.title: Page Break Element
docs.text:
Add a Page Break element to force content onto a new page:

  1. The Page Break element fills remaining space on the current page
  2. Content after the break appears on the next page

docs.title: Automatic Page Breaks
docs.text:
TemplateTo calculates estimated page breaks automatically. The editor shows dotted lines indicating where breaks will occur.

To disable this calculation (useful for templates with complex layouts), toggle "Disable PageBreak Calculation" in Template Settings.

Base64 Encoding

Raw HTML must be Base64 encoded. In JavaScript: btoa(htmlString). In Python: base64.b64encode(html_string.encode()).decode().

docs.title: Response Types
docs.text:
• File download - POST /render/pdf/{templateId} returns the PDF directly
  • Base64 encoded - POST /render/pdf/{templateId}/as-byte-array returns a Base64 string

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Test with realistic data - Use actual content lengths to verify page breaks
  2. Set appropriate margins - Leave room for headers/footers and binding
  3. Use content blocks - Share headers/footers across related templates
  4. Consider print settings - Enable "Print Background" if you use background colors
  5. Validate passwords - Test password-protected PDFs open correctly

docs.title: Plain Text Generation
docs.text: Render your templates as plain text (TXT) files. This is useful for email content, data exports, SMS messages, and any scenario where you need text without formatting.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Plain text output is ideal for:

  • Email body content (before HTML formatting)
  • SMS or notification messages
  • Data exports and reports
  • Integration with systems that only accept plain text
  • Generating configuration files or scripts

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When you render a template as TXT:

  1. All HTML elements are stripped
  2. Text content is extracted in reading order
  3. Variables are replaced with your data
  4. The result is returned as a plain text file

docs.title: Keep It Simple
docs.text:
For best results with TXT output, use templates that focus on text content:

  • Use Text elements for your content
  • Avoid complex layouts (columns will be flattened)
  • Tables will be converted to plain text (consider formatting)

docs.title: Variables Work the Same
docs.text:
All your variables and Liquid templating work identically:

Hello {{customerName}},

Your order #{{orderNumber}} has been shipped.

Items:
{% for item in items %}
- {{item.name}} (Qty: {{item.quantity}})
{% endfor %}

Total: {{total}}

Thank you for your business!

docs.title: Line Breaks
docs.text: Use the Page Break element or multiple Text elements to control line spacing in your output.

  -d '{"customerName": "Acme Corp", "orderNumber": "12345"}'

docs.text: Returns the text file directly with Content-Type: text/plain.

docs.title: Async Rendering
docs.text:

curl -X POST "https://api.templateto.com/render/async/txt/{templateId}" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: your-api-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customerName": "Acme Corp"}'

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Design for text first - If TXT is your primary output, keep templates simple
  2. Test the output - Preview as TXT to see how formatting translates
  3. Use consistent spacing - Control line breaks intentionally
  4. Consider character limits - For SMS, keep content concise
